title: Wedding Boxes
opening: Five kilos for a wedding. That is five times more than I have ever made.

intro.p: Rafiq Bhai's niece is getting married on Friday. The family wants gift boxes of Dadu's chocolate for every guest.

talk: Laila beta! My niece's wedding is on Friday. Five kilos of dark chocolate, in little boxes for the guests.
Five kilos? I have only ever made one.
Then it is five times the work, no? Easy.
Not exactly. Some things grow five times. Some things might not.
The family wants the darkest bar you can make. Ninety, they said. And a few toppings, for the sweet tooth.
Fine. I will read the order slip and Dadu's notes before I weigh anything.

lines.text: Scale the recipe to the big batch. Dark [[blur:ninety]] means that many of every hundred is cacao. [[torn:…weigh it, do not guess…]]
Conche it. [[q:Big pot or small, the stone turns all night.]]
Fill the sample tray the way the customer drew it. [[torn:…nothing wet goes in the chocolate…]]
Pour into the moulds. Tap the tray to knock the air out.

workshop.sceneAlt: Dadu's workshop with a wedding order on the table. Tap the glowing objects to remember.
workshop.hintLine: Tap the glowing spots. Dadu left clues all over the workshop.

clues.title: The wedding order
clues.text: Dark 90. Five kilos. Fifty grams a bar, one for every guest. Delivery on Friday.

artText.alt: An order slip: wedding order for Rafiq Bhai's niece, Dark 90, 5 kilos, 50 grams a bar, one for every guest, delivery on Friday

clues.title: Dadu's note on big batches
clues.text: "Big pot or small, the stone turns all night." He wrote it beside the conche in thick pencil.

artText.alt: Dadu's note on big batches: Big pot or small, the stone turns all night. Same night as always.

clues.title: The customer's sketch
clues.text: A drawing of a sample tray, four rows of five. The family has marked each square: plain, toasted dry coconut, or puffed rice.

artText.alt: The customer's sketch of a tray, four rows of five squares. row 1: toasted dry coconut, plain, plain, plain, toasted dry coconut; row 2: plain, puffed rice, toasted dry coconut, puffed rice, plain; row 3: plain, puffed rice, toasted dry coconut, plain, plain; row 4: puffed rice, plain, toasted dry coconut, plain, puffed rice
artText.legend: C coconut, R rice, P plain

clues.title: The toppings shelf
clues.text: Three jars: toasted dry coconut, puffed rice and a fresh coconut, still wet inside. Dadu stuck a note on the fresh one: "Not near the chocolate."

artText.alt: Three jars on a shelf: toasted dry coconut, puffed rice, and a fresh coconut with a note saying not near the chocolate

clues.title: The big scale
clues.text: Dadu weighed every batch twice. "Weigh it, do not guess," he said.

clues.title: A stack of gift boxes
clues.text: Flat-packed and tied with red string. The family sent a hundred of them.

artText.alt: A stack of flat gift boxes tied with red string

steps.title: Line 1: scale the recipe
steps.prompt: Work out the weights for the whole batch. Type a number in each box.
steps.say: Five kilos is a lot of cacao. The order slip says what kind of bar, how big the batch is and how big each bar is.

fields.label: Cacao (nibs)
fields.high: That is too much cacao. The bar would be harsher than the family asked for.
fields.low: That is too little cacao. The bar would be sweeter than a Dark 90.
fields.nearText: Close, but check your sum. Dark 90 means ninety of every hundred is cacao.

fields.label: Sugar
fields.high: That is too much sugar. It would not taste like a Dark 90.
fields.low: That is too little sugar. The bar would be harsh and bitter.
fields.nearText: Close, but check your sum. What is left of the batch after the cacao?

fields.label: Bars
fields.high: That is more bars than the batch can make. Each bar is the size on the slip.
fields.low: That is fewer bars than the batch can make. Each bar is the size on the slip.
fields.nearText: Close, but check your sum. How many bars of that size are in five kilos?

params.unfilled: Type a number in every box first.

feedback.correct: Forty-five hundred grams of cacao, five hundred of sugar, and a hundred bars. Everything is exactly five times, or so it seems.

hints: Read the wedding order in the Workshop. It gives the batch, the kind of bar and the size of each bar.
Five kilos is 5000 g. Ninety percent of it is 4500 g of cacao, which leaves 500 g of sugar. At 50 g a bar, that makes 100 bars.

steps.title: Line 2: conche
steps.prompt: Set how many hours the conche should turn for the big batch.
steps.say: Five times the chocolate. Surely that means five times the hours? Dadu wrote something about this.

feedback.correct: Eleven hours, the same night as always. A bigger pot does not need a longer night.
feedback.near: Close, but the note says the same night as always. Check the sign and the timetable from Chapter 1.
feedback.low: It will still be rough and sour. The stone needs the whole night.
feedback.high: That is far too long. The chocolate would go flat and dull. The stone only needs one night.

hints: Dadu's note about big batches is in the Workshop. The sign and the timetable from Chapter 1 are on the Memory shelf. Does a bigger pot need a longer night?
No. The stone turns all night: from 6 pm to 5 am, which is 11 hours, the same as for one kilo.

steps.title: Line 3: the sample tray
steps.prompt: Fill the tray to match the customer's sketch. Tap a topping, then tap a square. Or drag it there.
steps.say: Twenty squares, three toppings. The family drew exactly what they want.

toppings.name: Toasted dry coconut
toppings.says: Toasted dry coconut. Crisp, nutty and dry.

toppings.name: Fresh coconut
toppings.says: Fresh coconut. Soft and full of water.
toppings.reject: Fresh coconut is full of water. A few drops of water make chocolate seize, and Dadu's note on seizing says so. Use the toasted dry kind.

params.idleInfo: Tap a topping to hear about it.
params.pickFirst: Pick a topping first, then tap a square.

feedback.correct: Ten plain, five coconut, five puffed rice, just as the sketch shows.
feedback.wrongSquares: {n} squares do not match the sketch yet. Look at it again.
feedback.unfilled: Some squares are still empty. The sketch has a topping, or plain, in every square.
feedback.wrongOne: One square does not match the sketch yet. Look at it again.

hints: The customer's sketch in the Workshop shows what goes in each square.

Row 1: coconut, plain, plain, plain, coconut. Row 2: plain, rice, coconut, rice, plain. Row 3: plain, rice, coconut, plain, plain. Row 4: rice, plain, coconut, plain, rice. (Coconut means toasted dry coconut.)

steps.title: Last line: mould
steps.prompt: The chocolate is poured. Tap the tray six times to knock the air out.
steps.say: Pour, then knock the air out.

feedback.correct: The air is out. A hundred bars, ready to set.

talk: "A hundred bars, and every one of them dark as night. The family will be thrilled."
Can I carry a box to the wedding?
Five times the chocolate, and the same night in the conche. I learned something today.
recipe: 5 kg Dark 90: 4500 g cacao, 500 g sugar
Conche 11 hours, the same night as a small batch
Fill the sample tray as drawn: toasted dry coconut and puffed rice, never fresh coconut
Mould, tap out the air, and make 100 bars of 50 g
reveal.realFact: In real life, weights grow with the batch, but conching time depends on the machine and the style, so a bigger batch often needs longer. In this story, it is Dadu's own rule that the stone turns all night.
